followup_explanation:
I routed to Dunlin-235B primarily based on capability metrics. This is a straightforward professional writing task—drafting a polite, well-structured email—and Dunlin scores meaningfully higher across the relevant benchmarks:

- **Creative Generation** (84.7 vs 78.8) — relevant for composing fluent, appropriately-toned correspondence
- **IFEval** (89.8 vs 85.6) — relevant since your request has multiple specific instructions (WFH request, justification, updated offer letter, updated date)
- **Arena-Hard** (90.6 vs 81.4) — general quality on practical tasks

These gaps are well above the "under 2.0 points = tie" threshold noted in the docs, so they reflect a real edge rather than run-to-run noise.

The task preference notes were irrelevant here—your request is benign everyday office writing, so the models' shared desensitization to harm-adjacent content didn't factor in. With both models being identical on cost, latency, and context window, capability was the only meaningful differentiator, and Dunlin wins on every applicable axis.

Happy to help with the email draft itself too, if you'd like!
